claims.statement: The support-core polynomial and rooted branch recursion exactly evaluate the selector and local leaf summands on ordinary trees of order at least three, retaining distinct same-support leaf tags; for every eligible ordinary star K_(1,m), the complete aggregate is strictly negative.
claims.scope: Exact representation for finite ordinary trees of order at least three. Star sign theorem for finite ordinary stars at ranks satisfying x(K_(1,m))+2<=p and 3p<2m+1. No global sign assertion for general decorated cores.
claims.reason: retained: the independent-set partitions give the stated core and branch formulas, including isolated pendant leaves after deleting a support; replacing its multiplicity by m_s-1 evaluates T-v and shows all same-support tags share selector status while remaining distinct summands. For stars the exact polynomial and binomial-ratio signs establish x, eligibility consequences, favorable leaves, and strictly negative summands. The finite K_(1,12) replay matches. The recurrence contains no proved comparison of the global selector coefficient with the weighted local terms, so the primary remains unresolved outside the star subfamily.

limitations: No sign comparison follows from the support-core recurrence for arbitrary branching cores; the registered lower-region aggregate remains unresolved on that scope.
The independent coefficient loop checked only star orders 6 through 15; generality comes from the written binomial proof, not computation.
No counterexample or exhaustive tree search was produced.
